sents.t: Every morning, I go to the red coffee shop near my apartment.
Its name is Maple Café.
The barista is a young woman with short black hair.
Her name is Lily.
“Good morning, Sam! The usual?” she asks.
“Good morning, Lily. Not today. I want something new.”
I look at the menu on the wall.
It has many drinks: latte, cappuccino, iced coffee, hot chocolate, and tea.
“What is a latte?” I ask.
“It is coffee with a lot of hot milk,” Lily says.
“It comes in three sizes: small, medium, and large.”
“A medium latte, please. And a blueberry muffin.”
“That is six dollars and fifty cents.”
I pay with my card.
Next to the register, I see a small jar.
It says “Tips.” In America, people often give a tip.
I put one dollar in the jar.
I sit by the window with my latte.
It is hot and creamy.
Maple Café is my favorite place in Oakville.
